body.statement: If every block of \(C\) is a singleton, then \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\varnothing\) for all \(j\) and \(\mathcal R(C)\) is exactly the ordinary Markov-equivalence class of \(G\), with \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}=\delta\) as in Chickering1995. If no block of \(C\) is a singleton, then every edge is fixed and \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\) as in the BPEC identifiability boundary. If \(G=H\) and \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\), then \(\Pi=\Lambda\).
body.justification: The two extreme partitions verify that the characterization interpolates exactly between ordinary Markov equivalence and proper blocked identifiability.
body.gap: The two endpoint results are published separately by Chickering1995 and BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026; their exact interpolation within one full-model criterion is new.
body.consumer: These reductions provide regression tests for software and prevent interpreting every fixed arrow as a numerically identified direct effect.
body.proof_tex:
Suppose every block of \(C\) is a singleton. Then \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\varnothing\) for every \(j\), hence \(F(C)=\varnothing\). The static criterion in \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) reduces exactly to equality of skeletons and unshielded colliders. By \(\texttt{lem:verma-pearl-markov-equivalence}\), the graph coordinates in \(\mathcal R(C)\) are precisely the ordinary Markov-equivalence class of \(G\), and their parent partitions are forced to be all-singleton. The distance conclusion of the equivalence theorem gives \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D)\).

Now suppose no parent block of \(C\) is a singleton. For every edge \(i\to j\), the block \(B\in\mathcal N_j(C)\) containing \(i\) cannot belong to \(\mathcal N_i(C)\), since every member of the latter is contained in \(\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\) and no such set contains \(i\). Thus \(\mathcal N_i(C)\neq\mathcal N_j(C)\), so every edge lies in \(F(C)\). The static criterion fixes every orientation, and it fixes each nonsingleton family, which in this regime is the entire partition. Therefore \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\), consistently with \(\texttt{lem:bpec-proper-identifiability}\) on the proper BPEC subclass.

Finally assume \(G=H\) and \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\). The tangent-support lemma gives \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for every \(j\). The common graph gives identical parent sets. At each vertex the partition is uniquely reconstructed by adjoining singleton blocks for all parents outside the union of the common nonsingleton family. Hence \(\Pi_j=\Lambda_j\) for all \(j\), and \(\Pi=\Lambda\).
